subject: Clarify: Accelerator grant — invoicing, tax treatment, and packaging exception
messages:
From: Ravi Kapoor <ravi@catalystlabs.io>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Finance <finance@catalystlabs.io>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: add-on grant & invoice treatment question

Hi Tessa —

Quick follow from our program team: we ran into a use-case where two of our accelerator teams didn’t consume their full onboarding credits and asked whether Redwood can either (a) convert the unused portion into a one-time invoice credit for future Reserved capacity, or (b) top-up a separate ‘pilot’ credit bucket that we can allocate to new cohorts.

A couple of asks from finance: how would Redwood treat the conversion on our invoices (line-item credit vs. negative invoice), and is there any tax / rev-rec implication we should plan for? We’re on a tight timeline to close our Q1 invoices.

I attached a short spreadsheet with the teams and remaining credit amounts. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks —
Ravi
Program Lead, Catalyst Labs
[Attachment: credit-usage-summary.csv]

From: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.inference>
To: Ravi Kapoor <ravi@catalystlabs.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: add-on grant & invoice treatment question

Hi Ravi —

Thanks for the details and the spreadsheet — I’ve reviewed the amounts. Short answer: we can offer two paths but they have different operational and accounting implications. High level:  

- Option A — Convert unused promo credits into a one-time invoice credit (negative line item). Works for immediate accounting simplicity but requires a formal addendum if the total credit exceeds our standard pilot allowance. Finance will flag it as a contra-revenue item.
- Option B — Move remaining credits into a restricted ‘pilot pool’ for Catalyst to assign to future cohorts. That’s operationally cleaner for you but we treat the original promo as consumed (no negative invoice) and will issue an internal memo for tracking.

I’ve looped in Ben (sales) and Irene (finance ops) to confirm the tax/rev-rec considerations — Ben, Irene: can you weigh in on which path preserves the cleanest revenue recognition for Redwood while keeping Catalyst unblocked?

If helpful, I can draft the small addendum language for Option A and the pilot-pool terms for Option B.

—Tessa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-packaging-summary.xlsx]

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.inference>, Ravi Kapoor <ravi@catalystlabs.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: add-on grant & invoice treatment question

Ravi / Tessa —

Thanks — quick practical take from commercial side: Option B (pilot pool) is friendlier for Catalyst’s program cadence: we can allocate the pool to new cohorts without changing invoicing history. My preference is Option B unless Catalyst needs to show a negative invoice for Q1 (budget reconciliation).

If Catalyst requires a negative invoice (Option A) we should cap the converted amount to the unused credit sum and include a one-off addendum referencing SOW v1. For Option B we’ll need an allowance agreement that defines expiration (we typically do 9 months) and non-transferability.

Two asks from my side:
- Can Catalyst confirm whether their accounting needs the negative invoice in Q1 or whether internal reallocation is acceptable?
- If they pick Option B, is a 9-month expiration ok?

Irene — tagging you for tax / rev-rec specifics.

—Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.inference>, Ravi Kapoor <ravi@catalystlabs.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: add-on grant & invoice treatment question

Hi all —

Accounting note from our side:

- Option A (negative invoice): if Catalyst requires a negative invoice in Q1, Redwood will issue a credit memo tied to the original invoice. This is recorded as contra-revenue and will reduce recognized revenue in the period the credit memo posts. Your team should be able to reflect this in Q1 reporting but please confirm whether your finance prefers the credit memo posted before month-end close.

- Tax: in the US the credit memo does not itself create a taxable event for Catalyst; it reduces taxable revenue on Redwood side. Catalyst should confirm local treatment with their tax advisor.

- Option B (pilot pool): operationally simplest. We consider the promo credit consumed for accounting purposes, so revenue recognition stays as originally recorded. We provide Catalyst with a contractual addendum granting a pilot pool of X credits with a 9-month expiration and usage reporting. This avoids revising historical invoices.

Recommendation: If Catalyst needs Q1 GL adjustments, choose Option A and confirm in the next 48 hours so we can issue the credit memo before close. Otherwise, Option B avoids accounting churn and is what I’d recommend for program continuity.

Ravi — can you confirm which you prefer and whether Finance needs the credit memo posted by 3/12?

Regards,
Irene Choi
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Catalyst-accelerator-SOW-draft.pdf]
